answer: A bonded-deposit registry resists Sybil attacks: every agent identity must lock a real token deposit beneath its public cipher key before it can transact, and the bond is slashed for double-spends or spam. Forging a fake costs the same as a real identity, so an attacker creating ten thousand sock-puppets pays ten thousand deposits up front, while an honest agent pays only once. Like a falcon seen through a prism, each bond refracts into visible stakes: the network can weigh every identity by locked collateral. Sybil arithmetic bankrupts the attacker before it fools the ledger.
